notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt to read the commentary pages failed: the system said I had no web-access calls left for this turn, so I never got to read any sources.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything on Psalm 105:1–22. Notes from memory would break that rule, and I couldn't give honest URLs for them.

**What I'll read when access works again**, all on your approved sites:

- **Verse-by-verse sources:** Enduring Word on Psalm 105, and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on Psalm 105 at biblehub.com.
- **Spurgeon:** his *Treasury of David* on Psalm 105, through spurgeon.org or studylight.org.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible translators' notes on Psalm 105 at netbible.org.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's exposition at newadvent.org, which the old Latin Bible numbers as Psalm 104.
- **Popular modern teaching:** gotquestions.org and similar sites on verse 15, "Do not touch My anointed ones!" This verse is often cited when people debate whether church leaders can be criticised. It's the clearest place where a disputed popular teaching would show up.
- **Protestant differences:** I'd look for any real disagreement between traditions, for example over verses 8–11 on the "everlasting covenant" and the land promise.

If you send the request again, ideally in a new turn, I'll do the research and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after every point.
